messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 429 error rate for model_family=nebula-lite detected at 3923456789. 5m error_rate=8.4% (baseline ~0.2%). top callers: tenant=nu-983 (Nucleus Health), tenant=op-44. auto-throttle kicking in. Links: https://console.redwood/dashboard/alerts/3923456789

dana: seeing a customer-facing spike, Nucleus Health reporting failed requests. paging oncall.

samir: digging in dashboard now — requests/sec to nebula-lite jumped x6 at 02:11 UTC. possible traffic burst from scheduled job? https://console.redwood/queries/nebula-burst

ben: proposal: create a temporary per-tenant "quota bridge" for tenant=nu-983 to avoid mass 429s while we triage. Raise nebula-lite TPM 600 -> 1500 and RPM accordingly for 30m burst window. minimizes global pool impact. thoughts? :thinking_face:

eva: +1 for tenant carve. global raise risks starving lower-priority tenants. if we must, prefer tenant-scoped increase. also consider disabling funcall for that tenant to shave tokens.

dana: can we do tenant carve via admin API quickly? runbook section 4.2 covers per-tenant quota overrides. I'll stand by.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-112 "nebula-lite per-tenant 429 surge". Priority: P2. Pager duty notified.

alice: I'm oncall, taking lead. Preparing to apply override. Will post CLI used.

alice: ```bash
# apply per-tenant quota override (30m)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.local/admin/quota 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" 
 -d '{"tenant_id":"nu-983","model_family":"nebula-lite","override":{"tpm":1500,"rpm":30000,"duration_minutes":30}}'
```

ben: after applying, monitor 5m for side effects. set rollback trigger: increase in global queue wait time > 200ms or GPU headroom < 10%.

alice: applied override, API returned 200. override_id=ovr-2026-55. pasted into incident.

samir: metrics 4m post-change: 429 rate for nu-983 down from 42% of their requests to 2.1%, overall nebula-lite 429s down to 0.6%. P95 latency up ~80ms on nebula-lite (acceptable). :thumbsup:

eva: thanks. did we isolate any noisy job? any specific client culprit?

samir: preliminary: a data-backfill job from nu-983 kicked a parallel fan-out causing sustained bursts. CS says they started a large migration at 01:50 UTC.

dana: SRE check on capacity: GPU pool headroom across zones is 18% (safe). no OOMs. No other families degraded.

ben: configure automated rollback at +30m and add an early rollback condition: if global queue length > 500 for more than 2m.

alice: added rollback automation to override_id=ovr-2026-55. will monitor and manually intervene if triggers hit.

cs-bot: CS alert: pinged @cs-team and shared interim status for Nucleus Health. Suggested message: "We're throttling less for you while we finish the migration; we'll follow up."

dana: handoff: Alice monitoring until 02:50 UTC then I'll pick up for the 30m tail. Please keep incident notes concise. We'll run postmortem if customer impact > 5% of their requests or if rollback was forced.

samir: added runbook link and recommended follow-ups: (1) ask Nucleus to stagger workers, (2) consider permanent tenant SLA if they need sustained higher throughput, (3) evaluate pacing knobs in SDK. https://playbooks.redwood/nebula/overload

alice: noted — override auto-expire at 30m (scheduled). I'll post final metrics and close thread after revert.

dana: thanks team. if anything changes ping with urgent. :rotating_light:

alice: override removed at 3923456820, override_id=ovr-2026-55 revoked. final check: 429s stable at 0.3%, latencies back to baseline. closing incident note and creating follow-up ticket for CS + product to discuss quota uplift options.
